value.text:
Six arcs, chosen so that between them they account for the ground rather than leaving most of it outside any story. The sources document four modes, so the fourth arc is the survival squeeze and the fifth is the invasion alternative — leaving invasion out would have left a documented mode in no story at all.

epic E1 "Enter a round and take control of a ship"
note E1 "You pick one of four modes, appear beside the space station that is your base, and the ship answers the mouse or the keyboard. Nothing else in the game can happen until this has."
establishes E1 S:at_menu
requires E1 S:in_field
ground E1 "game mode"
ground E1 objective
ground E1 "space station"
ground E1 controls
ground E1 accelerate
ground E1 steer
ground E1 fire
ground E1 ship
ground E1 Fly
because E1 "the sources describe entering as three separable acts - choosing a mode, being placed, and gaining control - and a story that assumes any of them leaves a builder guessing"
instead E1 "starting the arc in the field, which would leave the mode choice and its objective unspecified"
state S:in_field "the pilot is flying in the field, under their own control"

epic E2 "Mine the belt until the hold is full"
note E2 "You shoot asteroids and the crystals they drop are worth something. Bigger rocks pay more per shot and cost more to stay near. The hold has a ceiling and crystals past it are simply lost."
establishes E2 S:in_field
requires E2 S:cargo_full
ground E2 asteroid
ground E2 gem
ground E2 "cargo capacity"
because E2 "a bounded hold is what makes returning to spend a decision instead of a formality"
instead E2 "an unbounded hold, which removes any reason to stop mining"
state S:cargo_full "the ship's crystal hold is full"

epic E3 "Convert a full hold into a better ship"
note E3 "A full hold goes into eight statistics, into an extra life, or into the next ship in the tree - and taking the next ship hands you an un-upgraded one. That trade is the decision the whole loop exists for."
establishes E3 S:cargo_full
requires E3 S:ship_stronger
ground E3 "spend gems"
ground E3 "upgrade categories"
ground E3 "upgrade cost"
ground E3 "extra life"
ground E3 tier
ground E3 "tier up"
ground E3 "energy regen"
because E3 "the sources give a full hold three destinations, and a story covering only the statistics would hide the choice that gives the tree its shape"
instead E3 "one destination, which would make a full hold a reward rather than a decision"
state S:ship_stronger "the ship is measurably better than it was"

epic E4 "Lose the hold, and then the ship, under fire"
note E4 "Shields absorb until they do not, and past that every hit knocks crystals out of your hold for anyone to take. Dying puts you back in a tier one ship with nothing."
establishes E4 S:in_field
requires E4 S:back_at_tier_one
ground E4 weapons
ground E4 shield
ground E4 "gems as shield"
ground E4 death
because E4 "the sources describe two separate losses - crystals bleeding out under fire, and the ship itself - and collapsing them into one would lose the reason a full hold is dangerous to carry"
instead E4 "loss only at death, which is what one of the two sources describes and is recorded as the open contradiction"
state S:back_at_tier_one "the pilot is flying again, back at tier one with nothing"

epic E5 "Survive the closing field until one pilot is left"
note E5 "A repulsive field grows out from the star and pushes everyone inward, warning as it goes. The round ends when one player remains."
establishes E5 S:in_field
requires E5 S:round_decided
ground E5 "gravity field"
ground E5 "endgame warning"
ground E5 "survival objective"
ground E5 "round end"
because E5 "a shrinking field forces contact without a clock deciding the round"
instead E5 "a round timer, which would end the game without anyone having to fight"

epic E6 "Hold the field against the invasion instead"
note E6 "One of the four documented modes replaces the last-survivor ending with waves of attackers and a final boss. It is a different arc to the same field, and leaving it out would leave a documented mode in no story."
establishes E6 S:in_field
requires E6 S:waves_cleared
ground E6 "invasion waves"
ground E6 "game mode"
because E6 "the sources document four modes, and an epic set that covers one of them describes a game narrower than the one being cloned"
instead E6 "covering survival alone, which is what the previous hand-written seed did"
state S:waves_cleared "the final wave has been beaten"
